correctness.rationale: For every \(p<q\le p^p\) and every positive periodic point, maximality gives \(a/p+b/q\le1\). Valuations outside the support are nondecreasing, so periodicity requires every \(aq+bp\) to have prime factors only from the support. With both supported valuations positive, the coefficient is greater than one and coprime to \(pq\), impossible. On the smaller-prime axis, smoothness leaves only \(a=1\) (vanishes after two steps) and \(a=p\) (fixed). On the larger-prime axis it leaves \(b=1\) (vanishes), \(b=q\) (fixed), or \(b=p^k<q\). The gap condition forces \(k<p\); the next derivative coefficient \(kq+p(p^k-1)>1\) is coprime to both primes, contradicting periodicity. A fixed maximum makes the whole orbit constant. The two explicit fixed families substitute directly. Finite verification only supplements this unrestricted symbolic argument.

value.rationale: The result resolves nontrivial periodic behavior uniformly for infinitely many prime pairs in the natural region \(q\le p^p\), extending the previously published isolated support {2,3}. It produces an intrinsic, exponentially strong necessary prime-gap obstruction from outside-prime monotonicity and a two-step maximal-orbit analysis. The explicit threshold is a mathematical consequence of the exponent \(k<p\) and is not an arbitrary finite slice; it materially narrows where longer cycles could be sought.
